# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024: 3B.10 research note

Bottom line: Tinubu inherited a difficult security environment, and he did make some de-escalatory and protective moves. But the year ended with lethal protest policing, mass detentions, treason charges, and continued evidence of unsafe conditions for children and conflict-affected people. On balance, I do **not** see clear evidence that citizens were left safer than they were inherited.

## Accepted claims

- [Tinubu launches national resettlement scheme for conflict victims](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-national-resettlement-scheme-for-conflict-victims/) — State House, July 6, 2024. Tinubu launched a resettlement scheme for conflict victims and framed it as rehabilitation and reintegration. This is the clearest positive evidence that he tried to reduce displacement and help victims of domestic insecurity. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`, `3B.9`.

- [Tinubu directs expeditious processing of welfare benefits, demands monthly KPI reports](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/) — State House, February 22, 2024. Tinubu ordered faster handling of welfare benefits and said delays to support for vulnerable citizens would not be tolerated. This is a positive anti-neglect signal, though it is administrative intent rather than evidence of measurable safety gains. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`, `3B.9`.

- [Tinubu establishes national education data system and approves skill development nationwide](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-national-education-data-system-and-approves-skill-development-for-all-levels-of-education-teacher-s-training-and-support-nationwide/) — State House, April 18, 2024. Tinubu approved child-focused education measures, including “academic security” and out-of-school-children interventions. This is positive for long-run safety of children, but it is indirect relative to violence reduction. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`.

- [Tinubu launches education campaign, says no child should be excluded from learning](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-launches-education-campaign-sys-no-child-should-be-excluded-from-learning/) — State House, May 13, 2024. Tinubu backed women’s rights, anti-GBV policy, and girls’ education in safe environments. This is positive evidence for protection of vulnerable groups, though it is still programmatic rhetoric. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`.

- [Tinubu asks protesters to suspend demonstrations, seeks dialogue](https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-tinubu-asks-protesters-to-suspend-demonstrations-seeks-dialogue/) — TheCable, August 4, 2024. Tinubu asked protesters to pause demonstrations to create room for dialogue. This is a real de-escalatory move, but it was reactive and did not prevent the violence that followed. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.8`, `3B.9`.

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. The government publicly offered dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence: some restraint, but also coercive preparedness that undercut the safety signal. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.5`.

- [President Tinubu calls for suspension of sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/) — State House, February 24, 2024. Tinubu urged negotiation and a “better path” over adversarial escalation in the ECOWAS crisis. This improved regional stability in a limited sense, but it does not by itself show domestic safety gains. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `2B.10`.

- [Tinubu signed four new nuclear safety regulations](https://www.nnra.gov.ng/nnra/post-president_tinubu_signs_four_new_nuclear_safety_regulations) — Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority, 2024. Tinubu strengthened nuclear safety and custody regulations, which is a narrow but real preventive-security gain. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `1B.3`, `1B.7`.

## Negative claims

- [Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Amnesty reported at least 24 deaths, mass detentions, and torture during the August protests. This is strong evidence that 2024 did **not** end with citizens safer from political violence. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.9`.

- [Nigeria charges protesters with treason, inciting military](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/) — Reuters via ThePrint, September 2, 2024. Prosecutors alleged protesters intended to destabilize Nigeria and incite mutiny. That frame escalated fear and helped justify coercion rather than improving public safety. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria charges 76, including minors, with treason after August protests](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nigeria-charges-76-including-minors-with-treason-after-august-protests-3698000) — Reuters via Investing.com, November 1, 2024. The government expanded treason charges to 76 people, including minors. This is strong evidence of punitive escalation and collective punishment after a spontaneous domestic flare-up. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.9`.

- [Nigeria: Protesters charged with treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) — Human Rights Watch, September 6, 2024. HRW said protesters, including children, were held for long periods with due-process concerns. This is strong evidence that domestic insecurity was not reduced in a rights-protective way. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`.

- [Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk) — Human Rights Watch, April 11, 2024. HRW said Nigerian authorities had failed to sustain measures for safe learning environments, leaving schoolchildren at continuing risk. This is negative evidence for the claim that Tinubu left children safer from preventable insecurity. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`.

- [Nigeria: Girls failed by authorities after escaping Boko Haram captivity](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/nigeria-girls-failed-by-authorities-after-escaping-boko-haram-captivity-new-report/) — Amnesty International, June 9, 2024. Amnesty found that girls and young women who escaped Boko Haram captivity faced unlawful detention and weak reintegration support. This is strong evidence against a broad safety improvement for vulnerable groups. Question IDs: `3B.10`; other: `3B.7`, `3B.2`.

## Assessment

- Positive evidence exists for resettlement, welfare processing, education policy, and limited de-escalation.
- The stronger evidence is negative: deadly protest policing, mass arrests, treason charges, and continuing danger for schoolchildren and Boko Haram survivors.
- I would rate the overall 2024 outcome as **mixed but net negative** on citizen safety.

## Search gap

- I did not find strong, quantified evidence that violence, deaths, displacement, or kidnapping materially fell nationwide in 2024.
- I also did not find clear evidence that communal, ethnic, or sectarian violence was substantially reduced across the year.
- Most available evidence is event-driven, especially around the August protests and Boko Haram-related vulnerability, rather than a clean year-over-year safety trend.
